Amblyopia, also known as lazy eye, is a condition where there is a reduction or loss of vision in one eye that is not caused by any eye disease. The good news is that visual loss in amblyopia is not always permanent. 

Research has shown that older people with a history of amblyopia who develop visual loss in the previously normal eye can experience recovery of visual function in the amblyopic eye over a period of time. This recovery in visual function occurs in the wake of visual loss in the fellow eye, and the improvement appears to be sustained. 

Therefore, while amblyopia can cause significant visual impairment, it is possible for the brain to rewire and adapt, leading to some level of visual recovery, even in adulthood. However, early detection and treatment of amblyopia are still crucial to prevent long-term vision problems.
